question: What is the main goal of Nigeria's National Reproductive Health Policy and Strategic Framework?

options.A: To reduce high rates of maternal and child mortality
options.B: To replace traditional birth attendants with medical doctors
options.C: To privatize all primary health care centers in the country
options.D: To increase the importation of foreign pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: You've got this! The core aim of this framework is to tackle the heavy burden of maternal and child deaths through coordinated health actions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why should student nurses care about the national reproductive health framework?

options.A: It allows them to practice independently without a supervising physician
options.B: It exempts them from clinical documentation requirements
options.C: It guarantees automatic promotion within the civil service
options.D: It ensures their local community nursing actions match national health goals

explanation: Spot on! Aligning everyday nursing care with national policies helps us all work together effectively to solve health challenges in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

options.C: Conducting forensic examinations for survivors of abuse
options.D: Screening for conditions like gestational hypertension

explanation: Great thinking! ANC visits give nurses a wonderful chance to monitor blood pressure and catch dangerous pregnancy complications early. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: A 30-week pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of a severe headache and blurred vision. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to eat more salt
options.B: Assess her blood pressure for signs of dangerous hypertension
options.C: Schedule her for routine tetanus vaccination next month
options.D: Encourage her to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: Well done! Severe headaches and vision changes are classic danger signs of preeclampsia. Checking her blood pressure right away is a life-saving priority. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?
explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is pre-contraception counseling so important in family planning clinics?

options.A: It is legally required before a patient can purchase over-the-counter condoms
options.B: It permanently prevents users from ever changing their chosen method
options.C: It helps clients choose a method that suits their lifestyle while addressing fears or myths
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical health assessment by a doctor

explanation: You nailed it! Good counseling clears up rumors about side effects and helps clients find the contraceptive method that best fits their personal life. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Health Services?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on the treatment of geriatric illnesses
options.B: Banning teenagers from visiting local community pharmacies
options.C: Providing confidential and accessible care without judgment
options.D: Requiring parental consent for every routine consultation

explanation: That's right! Youth-friendly centers remove barriers like judgmental attitudes and lack of privacy so young people feel safe seeking help. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do many teenagers shy away from standard healthcare clinics for reproductive health needs?

options.A: They fear harsh judgment, stigma, and a lack of confidentiality from staff
options.B: They prefer to use complex surgical procedures at home
options.C: They are completely unaware that health facilities exist in their towns
options.D: They are legally forbidden from entering government hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of being scolded or having their privacy broken stops many young people from getting the care they need early on. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: In Nigerian reproductive health programs, what does the acronym PMTCT stand for?

options.A: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Tumors
options.C: Public Midwifery Training and Community Testing
options.D: Postnatal Management of Teenage Children and Teens

explanation: You got it! PMTCT programs focus on stopping HIV from passing from an infected mother to her baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why do busy primary health centers often use syndromic management for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: It guarantees that laboratory scientists are no longer needed in hospitals
options.B: It allows nurses to treat common symptoms immediately using flowcharts before lab results return
options.C: It completely replaces the need for any physical examination of the patient
options.D: It is the only method approved by international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Brilliant! Syndromic management uses clear symptom guides so nurses can start treatment right away, which is a lifesaver when lab results take too long. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: A community midwife in a remote village is treating a woman with severe bleeding after childbirth who needs a blood transfusion. What should she do first?

options.A: Stabilize the patient with available fluids and arrange an immediate emergency referral
options.B: Ask the family members to perform minor surgery in the clinic ward
options.C: Wait until morning before telling anyone about the excessive bleeding
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to free up the hospital bed

explanation: You've got this! When an emergency is beyond the clinic's capacity, stabilize the patient with what you have and arrange a swift transfer to a higher center. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing reproductive health programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of surplus modern hospitals in every village
options.B: Shortages of trained healthcare staff in rural community clinics
options.C: Cultural or religious resistance to certain family planning methods
options.D: Financial barriers caused by out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: Spot on! Rural areas actually struggle with a lack of enough hospitals and clinics, making the idea of 'surplus hospitals in every village' completely false. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is it helpful to involve traditional and religious leaders in community health strategies?

options.A: They hold strong influence over community attitudes and can help promote health-seeking behaviors
options.B: They can write legal prescriptions for controlled narcotic medications
options.C: They control the central government budget for foreign medical equipment
options.D: They are legally trained to replace licensed medical doctors in emergency surgery

explanation: Brilliant! Local leaders are deeply respected; partnering with them helps clear up cultural myths and encourages community members to embrace healthcare. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)
